Fotocal vs Yazio: which calorie app to choose?

A dated, sourced comparison: what Yazio states on its site versus what Fotocal does, read off the app's code.

Updated: 8 November 2026 · By Fotocal, Madrid

Quick answer: Fotocal is an Android app that counts calories from a photo, built around Spanish food. Its free plan, with no card, includes 2 AI scans a day, 1 voice log a day, and unlimited barcode scanner and Coach Kal. Below is what Yazio states on its own site, checked on 10 September 2026.

Competitor columns show what each maker states on its own website, checked on 10 September 2026: ✓ or a plan name means the maker states it, — means it is not stated there. Prices are the makers' published yearly prices in US dollars and can change. Fotocal is Android-only for now. The Fotocal column is our own free and Premium line, read off the app rather than written by us: ✓ means the free plan with no cap, Premium means it needs a subscription, and anything else names the limit the free plan has.

What each row means

Which one to choose?

It depends on what you need. If you want to log what you eat from a photo, with Spanish food servings and without paying to start, that is what Fotocal is built for. If you use an iPhone, Fotocal is not available: it is Android only. If you already have years of logs in Yazio, the cost of switching counts too. Other apps' features and prices change: check their site before you decide.
